ledger.claim: The deviation is real and it is out of tolerance. The platform's own recorded distances put the actual route at 34.80 km against a recommended 32.40 km — a deviation of 2.40 km — and POL-RD-22 makes a deviation of 1.00 km or less within tolerance. At 2.40 km this detour is more than double the tolerance, so rows (c) and (e) of POL-RD-24, the within-tolerance 'no refund' rows, are closed to the driver.

The driver did not inform the rider of the deviation before or at the point of it, as POL-RD-21 requires. The chat log carries exactly two messages, both sent at 11:14, before the trip started at 11:16:14; the trip record's derived messages_during_trip array is empty, and trip_record.in_app_calls is empty, so there is neither an in-app notice nor any call recording of a verbal one. POL-RD-21's contact obligation is therefore unmet, and POL-GEN-26 confirms that a verbal notice with no recording in the record cannot be established. The rider never agreed to the reroute, so row (a) of POL-RD-24 is unavailable to the driver.

Nothing in the chat log can be read as the rider's agreement to a detour. Both entries concern the pick-up — the driver's 'at Jewel pick-up door 3, grey Kia Carnival' and the rider's 'Ok with 1 big luggage' — and both were sent before the trip began (11:14:04 and 11:14:54), whereas the route deviation was only detected at 11:45:45. POL-RD-21 treats the rider's acknowledgment as what makes a deviation agreed; a reply about luggage, sent half an hour before the detour, is not an acknowledgment of it.

The driver's own statement is an admission that he gave no notice: 'There was an accident on AYE, I avoid it. Didn't want to disturb the passenger, he was on his laptop.' Choosing not to disturb the rider is the opposite of POL-RD-21's duty to inform him of the deviation by in-app chat, or verbally with a call recording, before or at the point of deviation, and the driver does not claim he told the rider at any stage.

The traffic limb is not made out on this record. POL-RD-23 justifies a reroute only where a TRAFFIC_ADVISORY intersects the recommended route and overlaps the trip window, and it states that a driver's assertion of traffic with no such data does not justify the reroute. The LTA advisory does overlap the window (11:01:14 to 12:16:14 against a trip of 11:16:14 to 11:56:14) and is typed ACCIDENT, but its intersects_route and justifies_reroute values are null, and the derived block says in terms that the record does not say whether it lies on the recommended route. The intersection condition is therefore not established and the case falls in row (d) of POL-RD-24. If the judge instead finds the advisory justified the reroute, the driver's failure to inform puts the case in row (b) — and rows (b) and (d) award the rider the identical sum, so the rider recovers on either reading.

Whichever of rows (b) and (d) applies, the sum is the same: the excess distance fare, being the deviation distance times the metered per-km rate, without surge, rounded to the cent. That is 2.40 km x 0.92 SGD/km = 2.21 SGD — the very figure the fare breakdown's derived block records as excess_distance_fare_sgd. That is the refund the rider is entitled to on this trip's own numbers.

The rider is still carrying that sum. The fare was charged in full — total_charged 51.32 SGD against distance_charged_km 34.80, payment_status CHARGED — and refund_issued_sgd is 0.00. Under POL-GEN-03 a PARTIAL_REFUND of 2.21 SGD is what returns the deviation's cost to the rider, whereas NO_ACTION leaves the present state standing, which here means the rider paying for 2.40 km he was given no chance to refuse.

This is a case the AI can decide, so the rider should have the money rather than a hold. POL-RD-25 sets the bar at a POL-GEN-22-permitted ruling at a confidence of 0.80 or more, and the 2.0 km limb of v2.1 6.2 is held and not applied (thresholds.ai_ruling_max_deviation_applied is false), so a 2.40 km deviation does not force escalation. The disputed value of 30.00 SGD sits in POL-GEN-22's 10.00 to 50.00 band, giving a required confidence of 0.80, and no fraud flag is carried on either profile to raise it to 0.95; every artifact relied on above is COMPLETE at weight_multiplier 1.0, so nothing in POL-GEN-02 caps that confidence either.

The reroute itself was permitted and is traffic-justified on the record. POL-RD-21 allows a driver to leave the recommended route in response to real-time traffic, and POL-RD-23 requires the justification to come from traffic data rather than the driver's word. The platform-retrieved LTA advisory LTA-TI-260929-3650 is exactly that data: an ACCIDENT (an admissible incident type) on the Ayer Rajah Expressway towards Tuas, after the Lower Delta Road exit, valid 11:01:14 to 12:16:14, which encloses the trip window 11:16:14 to 11:56:14. The recommended route runs on the AYE. The trip record's own events place the vehicle leaving the recommended AYE at the Lower Delta Road exit at 11:45:45 and rejoining the AYE at the Portsdown Road slip road at 11:53:23. On the advisory's own stated road, direction and location, the incident lies on the AYE segment the driver bypassed, travelling the same direction the trip was travelling. The driver's account is therefore corroborated by third-party data, not left as a bare assertion, and the reroute is traffic-justified.

The deviation must be measured the POL-RD-22 way, and it comes to 2.40 km. POL-RD-22 fixes the deviation as trip_record.actual_distance_km minus trip_record.optimal_distance_km on the platform's recorded distances, and expressly does not re-measure from the GPS trace, which is sparse and understates the route. On the record: 34.8 km actual less 32.4 km recommended. That is over the 1.0 km tolerance (within_tolerance is false), so the case cannot fall in POL-RD-24(c) or (e), and the refund is determined by the excess distance fare rather than by the trip fare.

The driver does not press for NO_ACTION, because the record does not establish that the rider was informed of the deviation before or at the point of deviation. POL-RD-21 requires in-app chat notice, or a verbal notice carried by a trip call recording, and a verbal notice with no recording cannot be established. Here the chat log's last entry is 11:14:54, before the 11:16:14 trip start; the trip record's messages_during_trip is empty; in_app_calls is empty; and the driver's own statement is that he did not want to disturb the passenger. Notice is therefore not made out and the deviation is not 'agreed' under POL-RD-21, so POL-RD-24 row (a) is unavailable. That concession is the whole of the driver's fault on the contact obligation, and it leaves the case in row (b): traffic-justified, rider not informed, deviation over 1 km.

On the facts so found, the rider's recovery is the excess distance fare and nothing more. POL-RD-24 computes it as the deviation distance times fare_breakdown.per_km_rate_sgd, without surge, rounded to the cent: 2.40 km x 0.92 SGD/km = 2.21 SGD, which is the ledger's own excess_distance_fare_sgd figure. POL-GEN-03's PARTIAL_REFUND returns part of the charge, and that part is 2.21 SGD — not the 30.00 SGD contested. The rider's request of 30.00 SGD is not a measure POL-RD-24 provides for a traffic-justified reroute, and the rider's assertion that the fare was higher than usual is not a ground of entitlement: the metered fare was computed on the recorded 34.8 km and 40.0 minutes at the rate card. Critically, the figure is the same on either reading of the traffic question — POL-RD-24(b) and (d) both pay the whole excess distance fare — so even if the judge declined to find the advisory intersects the recommended route, the rider's ceiling is still 2.21 SGD. There is no route on this matrix to 30.00 SGD.

Nothing on the driver's side rests on impaired evidence, and the case is ruleable. The trip record, the driver-device GPS trace, the chat log, the fare ledger and the LTA advisory are each COMPLETE with weight_multiplier 1.0, so POL-GEN-02's cap on confidence is not engaged and no issue code needs to be named. The recorded deviation of 2.40 km is above POL-RD-25's 2 km figure, but that limb is held in route_deviation.thresholds.ai_ruling_max_deviation_applied, which is false, so it is not applied and does not force escalation. The dispute value is 30.00 SGD, inside POL-GEN-22's 10.00 to 50.00 band, so the ruling stands at a confidence of 0.80 or more, and on this record that confidence is available: the traffic justification is carried by contemporaneous third-party advisory data and the distance by the platform's own recorded distances.

ruling.explanation:
The rider filed this dispute, so the outcome is read against the rider's claim on trip TRP-06009.

How far the driver went off route (POL-RD-22). POL-RD-22 measures the deviation from the platform's own recorded distances, not from the sparse GPS trace. The record gives 34.80 km actual against 32.40 km recommended — a deviation of 2.40 km. The tolerance is 1.00 km, so this detour is more than double it. The within-tolerance 'no refund' rows of the refund matrix are therefore closed to the driver, and this is common ground between the parties.

Was the reroute traffic-justified (POL-RD-23). Yes. The platform-retrieved LTA advisory LTA-TI-260929-3650 records an ACCIDENT on the Ayer Rajah Expressway towards Tuas, after the Lower Delta Road exit, valid 11:01:14 to 12:16:14, which encloses the trip window 11:16:14 to 11:56:14. ACCIDENT is an admissible incident type. The recommended route runs on the AYE and the trip was heading towards Tuas; the vehicle left the AYE at the Lower Delta Road exit at 11:45:45 and rejoined at the Portsdown Road slip road at 11:53:23. The incident, on the AYE just past the Lower Delta Road exit in the direction of travel, lies on exactly the stretch the driver bypassed, so the advisory intersects the recommended route the driver left. I reject the rider's alternative reading that the traffic limb is unproven — the advisory's own road, direction and location, read against the trip, place it there. In any event the point does not change the money: rows (b) and (d) of POL-RD-24 return the same sum.

Was the rider told (POL-RD-21). No. The chat log holds two messages (11:14:04 and 11:14:54), both before the trip started and both about the pick-up, not a detour; the trip record shows no messages during the trip and no call recordings; and the driver's own statement — 'Didn't want to disturb the passenger, he was on his laptop' — is a concession that he gave no notice. POL-RD-21 requires notice before or at the point of deviation, and a verbal notice with no recording cannot be established (POL-GEN-26). Notice is not made out, the rider never agreed, and row (a) is unavailable.

What is owed (POL-RD-24, POL-GEN-03). The case sits in row (b): traffic-justified, rider not informed, deviation over 1 km. The matrix refunds the excess distance fare — the deviation distance times the metered per-km rate, without surge: 2.40 km x 0.92 SGD/km = 2.21 SGD, which is the fare ledger's own excess_distance_fare_sgd figure. The rider asked for 30.00 SGD of the 51.32 SGD fare, but POL-RD-24 provides only the excess distance fare; the metered fare was computed on the recorded 34.80 km and 40.0 minutes and the matrix does not return the whole trip fare. So of the 30.00 SGD contested, 2.21 SGD is owed, as a PARTIAL_REFUND. The fare is confirmed CHARGED with refund_issued_sgd 0.00, so the rider still carries this sum.

Why the ruling can stand (POL-RD-25, POL-GEN-22, POL-GEN-02). No artifact the ruling relies on is impaired — the trip record, GPS trace, chat log, fare ledger and LTA advisory are each COMPLETE at weight_multiplier 1.0, so nothing caps confidence below the bar. The dispute value of 30.00 SGD sits in POL-GEN-22's 10.00 to 50.00 band, requiring a confidence of 0.80, and no fraud flag is carried on either profile to raise it to 0.95. The 2.0 km limb of v2.1 6.2 is held and not applied (thresholds.ai_ruling_max_deviation_applied is false), so the 2.40 km deviation does not force escalation.

No referral is produced: a route deviation has no referral clause in this version.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
